newsitem.title: FRANCE: French express firms welcome court Chronopost ruling.
newsitem.headline: French express firms welcome court Chronopost ruling.

text.p: French express operators said a decision by the Paris Commercial Court that it was competent to judge a case opposing the express operators association (SFEI) and Chronopost, the express arm of the French post office, was a "further victory".

The long-running case, which has also been before the European Commission and the European Court of Justice, centres on SFEI claims that the French post office provided aid representing some 850 million francs to Chronopost during 1986-1991 in contravention of EU competition rules.
SFEI also claims private express operators market share was affected by this aid to Chronpost and this represented a financial prejudice of some 216 million francs.
"We have consistently argued that a commercial court was the right place for this case to be heard and this has been upheld.

"We will now have the right platform to put our case that the post office was abusing its monopoly status in aiding Chronopost to developing its activities in a competitive market," an SFEI official told Reuters.

Commenting on the court's decision, Chronopost said in a statement: "The court has deemed itself competent to judge the case despite the post office being under public administration until 1990 and contrary to the view expressed by the public prosecutor's during the hearing " that the court did not have the power to do so.
The SFEI official said the court had ordered Chronopost to pay 100,000 francs to SFEI in legal costs and had fixed a hearing for May 13. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
